chain.reference_token: unrealizable: The row needs a restored prevout already present in the coins view at undo time. Disconnection runs from the tip down and, within a block, in reverse transaction order; for an unmodified body an undo entry restores the spending input's own prevout. The implemented rev-record edits change restored data, not that prevout or pre-existing coins. This harness has no chainstate writer or block-body corruption instrument. The stopped-datadir surface could in principle support either: disk reads check header proof of work and the indexed header hash without recomputing the body's merkle root, and checklevel=0 skips block validity checks. A body-prevout replacement is an unmeasured candidate; its changed transaction id can also cause an output-removal mismatch, which must be controlled before an isolated collision is counted. At the pin a block's freeze is assigned when its own connection spends a consensus-frozen output. The duration setter rejects negatives but has no upper bound: literal zero maps to INT32_MAX, while nonzero int64 values narrow into an int32 field. On the pinned build's ordinary conversion, 4294967296 narrows to zero; the block is frozen but its child receives -1 and is not effectively frozen. This source-derived boundary is unmeasured. It does not supply the row's explicit set/clear route on an already-active block: no supported RPC clears the persisted block mark; clearing blacklist entries is a different operation.
